keyword: how to write a diary about myself
title: How to Write a Diary About Myself (With 40 Prompts)
description: How to write a diary about myself: steps for writing about your day and feelings, honest examples, and 40 prompts to get to know yourself. Write here free.
h1: How to write a diary about myself
intro: To write a diary about yourself, write the date, then describe one thing that happened today and how it made you feel. Ask yourself why you felt that way, and end with what you learned or what you need. Be honest, because nobody else is reading. A few true lines about you are worth more than a page of what you think you should say.

writer.title: Dear me,
writer.hint: How am I really doing today?

sections.h2: How to write a diary about myself in 6 steps

steps.name: Pick a private place to write
steps.text: You will only be honest if you feel safe. Use a notebook you can keep somewhere private, or a private online diary like the one on this page.

steps.name: Write the date and how you feel in one word
steps.text: Tired. Hopeful. Annoyed. Calm. One word is a quick check in and helps you see patterns when you read back.

steps.name: Write about one moment from today
steps.text: Not the whole day. Pick the moment that stuck with you. What happened, who was there, what was said.

steps.name: Ask yourself why
steps.text: Why did that moment matter? Why did it make you feel that way? This is where you start learning about yourself.

steps.name: Notice what you need
steps.text: Rest, a talk with a friend, some time alone, a plan, a treat. Write it down.

steps.name: Close kindly
steps.text: End with something you did well today, or something you are looking forward to. Write to yourself like you would to a good friend.

blocks.tip: Starting is the hardest part. If you are stuck, write "Right now I feel..." and finish the sentence. Keep going from there.

sections.h2: How to write a diary about your day

blocks.p: Writing about your day is the easiest way to start writing about yourself, because the day gives you the story. The trick is to add **you** to it: not only what happened, but what you thought and did.

head: Just the facts
About you
rows: I dragged myself to work. Mondays always feel heavy.
Lunch with Tom was the best part. I always feel lighter after we talk.
I watched TV for three hours to avoid thinking about the exam.

example.label: About my day
example.title: Dear me,
example.text:
Today was busy and I said yes to too many things.
I helped Jess with her project, then stayed late for a meeting.
By dinner I felt grumpy and snapped at my brother.
I think I was not angry at him. I was tired.
I need to practice saying "not today" without feeling guilty.
One good thing: the sky on the way home was pink and gold.

sections.h2: How to write a diary about your feelings

blocks.p: Feelings can be hard to put into words. These simple moves help:

ul: **Name it.** Use a specific word. Not just bad, but lonely, embarrassed, disappointed or overwhelmed.
**Find it in your body.** Tight chest, heavy shoulders, a lump in your throat. Writing where you feel it helps you notice it sooner next time.
**Find the trigger.** What happened just before you felt this way?
**Let it be messy.** Write in fragments if you want. A diary is not an essay.
**Ask what it is telling you.** Anger can mean something felt unfair. Sadness can mean you miss something that mattered.

example.label: About my feelings
example.title: Dear diary,
example.text:
I feel left out tonight.
Everyone posted photos from the party and I was not invited.
My stomach dropped when I saw them.
I think it hurts because I want to feel like I belong there.
Maybe I can invite Lily and Ana over next weekend myself.
It is okay to feel this. It will pass.

blocks.p: If you want to track feelings over time, a [mood journal](/mood-journal/) can help you spot patterns.

blocks.tip: A diary can help you sort through hard feelings, but it is not a replacement for professional care. If you feel overwhelmed for a long time, talk to someone you trust or a doctor. If you are in crisis, contact local emergency services. In the US, call or text 988.

blocks.p: Press **Write** to open any prompt in the diary at the top.

prompts: Describe yourself in five words, then explain each one.

Write about a time you felt completely safe.
What would you say to a friend who felt the way you feel now?

What is a memory that shaped who you are?
What did you love doing as a child that you have stopped doing?

What is the hardest thing you have been through, and what did it teach you?
What is a decision you are glad you made?

blocks.p: For even more questions like these, see our [journal prompts for self discovery](/journal-prompts-for-self-discovery/).

sections.h2: Tips for honest writing about yourself

ul: **Write as if no one will ever read it.** Then make sure no one can. Keep the diary private.
**Do not edit while you write.** Get the thoughts out first. Spelling does not matter.
**Be fair to yourself.** Write about mistakes, but also write about what you did well.
**Notice repeats.** If the same worry shows up every week, that is worth paying attention to.
**Read back once a month.** You will see how you have grown, and what still needs care.
**Keep it short on hard days.** One line like "Today was hard and I got through it" is enough.

blocks.p: New to diaries? Start with [how to write a diary](/how-to-write-a-diary/), browse [diary ideas](/diary-ideas/), or read real [diary entry examples](/diary-entry-examples/) to see what others write.

faq.q: How do I write a diary about myself?
faq.a: Write the date and how you feel in one word. Then describe one moment from today, ask yourself why it affected you, and write what you need. End with something kind to yourself. Be honest and keep it private. A few true lines are a complete entry.

faq.q: How do I start a diary about my feelings?
faq.a: Start with the sentence Right now I feel, and finish it with a specific word like lonely, nervous or relieved. Then write what happened just before you felt that way and where you feel it in your body. Let it be messy. You can make sense of it later.

faq.q: What should I write about myself in a diary?
faq.a: Write about your day, your feelings, your worries, your hopes, your memories and the people who matter to you. You can also write about what you like and dislike, what you are proud of and what you want to change. Prompts help when you do not know where to begin.

faq.q: Is it good to write a diary about your feelings?
faq.a: Many people find it helps. Research on expressive writing has found that putting feelings into words can help some people process stress and see things more clearly. It is not a replacement for professional care if you are struggling, but it can be a helpful daily habit.

faq.q: How do I write about my day in a diary?
faq.a: Pick the moment that stuck with you most, write what happened, and then add how you felt and why. Adding your thoughts turns a list of events into a diary about you. If the day was busy, write three lines: what happened, how it felt, one thing to remember.
